title: Representation of the derived product of a tower
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. Choose a complex $C_\bullet$ of towers representing $M_\bullet$ and a K-injective resolution
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge] $C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ in the abelian
category of towers. Write $M_n=\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$. Then the derived product $R\!\prod_nM_n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is represented by
$\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$.

Here the product complex is formed in $\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)$, and is read in its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; its degree-$q$ term is $\prod_{n\geq1}(\operatorname{ev}_nI_\bullet)^q$, with differential determined by its composites with the projections. The source is Stacks Tag 07KC (label lemma-products): exact countable products allow termwise products of any representatives. Tag 0BK6 is an alternative when the individual representatives are known to be K-injective; that additional assertion is not needed here.

proof.text: Evaluation of a morphism of tower complexes at each index preserves quasi-isomorphisms by Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_iff_evaluation (equivalently, exact evaluation preserves homology). DerivedCategory.Q inverts these morphisms. NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app proves pbcComplexEvaluation_inverts, so the localization lift and its comparison isomorphism give the specified derived evaluation.

Apply lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact to the actual completed commutative coefficient sheaf completedAdicCommRing T d. Its underlying ring sheaf is definitionally completedAdicRing T d. The epimorphism statement makes the countable limit functor preserve epimorphisms: conjugate its map by Pi.isoLimit to the product of the component maps. Mathlib hasExactLimitsOfShape_of_preservesEpi and CountableAB4Star.of_hasExactLimitsOfShape_nat give exact countable products. Finite biproducts come from the abelian module-sheaf category.

Apply derivedCategory_countableProducts_core to CompletedAdicModules T d. Its first conclusion supplies HasCountableProducts in the derived category. For C(n)=I.asFunctor.obj(op n), its second conclusion supplies a limiting localized product cone. Fan.isLimitMapConeEquiv expresses this as the fan with projections Q.map(Pi.π C n).

For each n, compose the inverse evaluation-comparison isomorphism at I with the image under pbcDerivedEvaluation of e, then evaluate at op n. Discrete.natIso assembles these isomorphisms. IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv transports the limit property along them. Fan.ext with the identity vertex isomorphism identifies the resulting fan with pbcRepresentativeProductFan: its n-th projection is exactly Q.map(Pi.π C n), followed by the inverse evaluation comparison and then evaluation of the image of e.hom. This proves the given statement; the K-injectivity hypothesis is not needed because Tag 07KC applies to every representative.

lean.statement: theorem pbcDerivedProductRepresentation (d : Scheme.AdicCoefficientDatum A) : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicModules T d)) ∧ ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d)) (I : CochainComplex (Scheme.CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ) (_hI : I.IsKInjective) (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj I ≅ M), Nonempty (IsLimit (pbcRepresentativeProductFan T d M I e))

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$ with a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ in the abelian
category of towers. Then the derived product $R\!\prod_nM_n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is represented by
$\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] the derived product $R\!\prod_nM_n$
is the product of the system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ in the
triangulated category $D(T_{\Proet},A)$ attached to the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Clause (2) of the derived-limit
existence lemma of the conventions chapter states that in the derived
category of an abelian category with exact countable products the countable
products exist and are represented by termwise products of any
representatives, and clause (3) of the same lemma exhibits
$\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ as the termwise product of the
K-injective representatives $\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ of the objects
$\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$; hence that product represents
$R\!\prod_nM_n$.
